CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  DEVELOPMENT SERVICES DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
February 7, 2024, 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor
1 West Manchester Boulevard
 ----------------------------------------------------------------
1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minutes approval for  January  10,  2024,  Special  Planning
  Commission meeting.

6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by David Nola,
  representing Social Pies for Special Use Permit No. 23-00026
  (SUP23-00026) to allow the on-site consumption of alcoholic
  beverages(beer,  wine  and  distilled  spirits)  in  an
  approximately 1,918 square-foot sit-down restaurant that is

  South District Drive.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2024-005; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SUP23-00026,
  subject to 13 conditions.
  Item 6a Documents

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by John Fox,
  representing Wireless Development Resources, LLC, for Special
  Use Permit No. 23-00030 (SUP23-00030) to allow the location
  of a 69-foot high, wireless telecommunication facility (mono-
  eucalyptus)  on  an  existing  shopping  center  site
  approximately  1.37  acre  and  zoned,  M-1L  (Limited
  Manufacturing) at 3550 W. Century Boulevard.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2024-012; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SUP23-00030,
  subject to 23 conditions.
  Item 6b Documents

7.  NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by
  Deborah Han, representing Kaiser Permanente, for Design
  Review No. 23-00037 (DR23-00037) to allow a proposed
  mural and exterior alterations on an approximately
  63,400 square-foot 4-story commercial building, on an
  H-C (Historic Core)zoned property at 110 North La Brea
  Avenue.
   Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2023-105; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR23-00037,
  subject to 8 conditions.
  Item 7a Documents

  b. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Chima
  Chibueze for Design Review No.23-00084 (DR23-00084) to
  allow a proposed mural on an approximately 11,681 square-
  foot commercial building (operating as a night club), on
  an MU-1 (TOD Mixed Use 1) zoned property at 446 South
  Market Street.

  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2024-015; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving DR23-00084,
  subject to 7 conditions.
  Item 7b Documents

8.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

9.  Commission Initiatives.

10.  Adjournment.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 7, 2024

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, February 7, 2024, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Carolyn Fowler
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson Sr., DSD Director
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Acting Planning Manager
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Assistant Planner
  Cynthia Robinson, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. Jackson stated that he was excited to present the Acting
Planning Manager for the meeting, a thirty-five year, plus
servant of the City of Inglewood, Mr. Eddy Ikemefuna. He stated
that Mr. Ikemefuna has been a tremendous asset to him and he is
proud to have him serve in this capacity for the evening.

Mr. Jackson also gave an update on the activity in the retail
area of Hollywood Park. He stated that the Cinepolis Luxury
theaters are open and operational. The Iconic Fitness Gym is
under construction and will be open soon. He also listed, Phoenix
Salon Studios, Google Code Next, Antojitos Martin, Smize, J.D.
Sports, Red Bay Coffee, Cosm, Grilled Fraiche, Resident Art
Gallery, Verizon, Social Pies, Coco Breezy, and Three Weavers
Brewery will all be coming soon. Mr. Jackson stated that in Sales
Folks, Puppy and Rose, Tilt, Sabrak Boutique, Pandora, Fixin’s,
Impact Hospitality and an unnamed National Restaurant are all in
negotiations.

Mr. Jackson stated that the forms 700 are due now.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

(5) MINUTES:
Chairman Springs called for Minutes approval for the January 10,
2024, Special Planning Commission meeting.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams made the motion to approve the January
10, 2024, Special Planning Commission Minutes and was seconded
by Commissioner Fowler.

Ayes: Commissioners Fowler, Rice, Shaw-Williams, and Chairman
  Springs.

Abstained: Commissioner Trejo
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 7, 2024

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. (SUP-23-00026)1245 SOUTH DISTRICT
DRIVE: A public hearing to consider an application by David Nola,
representing Social Pies, for Special Use Permit No. 23-00026 (SUP-
23-00026) to allow the on-site consumption of alcoholic beverages
(beer, wine and distilled spirits) in an approximately 1,918
square-foot sit-down restaurant that is part of a multiple-tenant
commercial building located in the Hollywood Park retail center on
an approximately 1.53-acre, HPSP (Hollywood Park Specific Plan)
zoned property at 1245 South District Drive.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the Staff Presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
 Was there any written communication from the public on this
  project?
  -Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Fowler’s question.

 Commissioner Rice asked staff -
 Are there five approved alcoholic distribution places within
  this census track?
 Do you know what the population is in this census tract?
   Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Will the same menu be available for the bar area?
  -Mr. Salazar responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs invited the applicant to come  before  the
Planning Commission to speak about the project.

David Nola, representing Social Pies  addressed  the Planning
Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
 Is this a chain?
 Do you have alcohol in the other locations?
 What additional security methods are you planning to provide?
 Will your facility have additional cameras as well?
  -Mr. Nola responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Did you mention a number of your stores are seeking
  entitlements for alcohol distribution?
 So the experience that Social Pies has with distributing
  alcohol is about nine months?
  -Mr. Nola responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 What kind of training will your servers and/or suited security
  guards have to determine who has been overserved?
 How many security guards will be on site?
 Is there one security guard at the door?

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
February 7, 2024

  In the event a person comes in that is overserved how will the
  security handle that?
  Are there plenty of resources in the center that in the event
  of any unruly the restaurant can reach out to?
  -Mr. Nola responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo stated that she would like to commend them on
not having live entertainment or amplified music.

Mr. Salazar stated that there is an IPD substation located within
the parking structure adjacent to the retail center.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –
 Will there be take-out service?
 Will you validate?
 Are you going to consider an Inglewood or City of Champions
  style pizza?
  -Mr. Nola responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
 Where are the stores located that do not have alcohol license?
 Did you submit for alcohol license at those locations?
 Is it safe to say that by serving alcohol it will bring a
  better price tag for your restaurant?
 How would the community benefit from you having a liquor
  license and serving alcohol in your restaurant?
 Is it a possibility that you can have a pizza that recognizes
  the City itself?
 Your specialty is pizza?
 Does alcohol go with pizza?
  -Mr. Nola responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

FOR/AGAINST:
None.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked if there
were any further questions from the Planning Commission. Seeing
none, Chairman Springs called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Trejo made a motion to affirm categorical exemption
EA-CE-2024-005; and adopt the attached resolution approving SUP-
23-00026 subject to 13 conditions plus 2 additional conditions
1) That no live entertainment or amplified music shall be
permitted and 2) That a City of Inglewood Pizza be created and
served at the restaurant and was seconded by Commissioner Shaw-
Williams, that Resolution No. 1981

  1,918 SQUARE-FOOT, SIT DOWN RESTAURANT THAT IS
  PART OF A MULTIPLE TENANT COMMERCIAL BUILDING

  A MIXED-USE DESIGNATED HPSP (HOLLYWOOD PARK

6B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 23-00030 (SUP-23-00030)1713-1717
CENTINELA AVENUE: A public hearing to consider an application by
John Fox, representing Wireless Development Resources, LLC, for
Special Use Permit No. 23-00030 (SUP23-00030) to allow the
location of a 69-foot high, wireless telecommunication facility
(mono-eucalyptus)  on  an  existing  shopping  center  site
approximately 1.37 acre and zoned, M-1L (Limited Manufacturing)
at 3550 West Century Boulevard.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
 In the photo the tree is not covering the tower, is that what
  your condition is?
   Mr.  Leon-Martell  responded  to  Commissioner  Fowler’s
  question.

Commissioner Rice stated that he wanted to commend the Planning
Department  for  listening  to  their  concerns  and  making
adjustments.

Commissioner Trejo commented that she was glad that staff added
that condition to make sure that the antenna is completely
covered.

Chairman Springs asked the Applicant to come before the Planning
Commission to speak about the project.

John Fox, representing Wireless  Development  Resources,  LLC
addressed the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Fowler asked the Applicant –
 Are there residential properties in the area as well?
 Will those areas be covered?
  -Mr. Fox responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked the Applicant –
 Provided this application is approved, how long will it take
  to get this built and in service?
Commissioner Rice commented that this is well needed.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the Applicant –
 How do you determine when you need to add tower that will best
  serve the community?
  -Mr. Fox responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant –

 You indicated you have photographs of another location, can we

 Is the first one an Oak tree?

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 Will the design facing La Brea be backlit?
Commissioner Trejo commented that she wanted to say thank you for
the explanation on including the Palm trees in the design. She

7B. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 23-00084 (DR-23-00084)446 SOUTH MARKET
STREET: A non-public hearing to consider an application by Chima
Chibueze for Design Review No. 23-00084 to allow a proposed mural
on an approximately 11,681 square-foot commercial building
(operating as a night club), on an MU-1 (TOD Mixed Use 1) zoned
property at 446 South Market Street.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner  made  the  Staff
Presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 This mural was put on prior to the applicant being aware that
  they were required to have an application?
 Was the signage permitted?
 This tenet just occupies the 4,700 square-foot night club?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Can you provide some of the conditions that were proposed on
  some of the earlier applications?
 Can you tell me if we required them to do something to the
  wall to make it look nicer?
 Can you tell me if we required them to do something to the
  wall to make it look nicer?
 Can the design review require that they do more to the façade
  to make it look more aesthetically pleasing?
  - Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Commissioner Trejo’s
  questions.

Chairman Springs commented that he loves the mural and thinks the
design is beautiful.
Chairman Springs asked staff –
 What is north of the building?
  - Mr. Leon-Martell responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Mr. Jackson responded to Chairman Spring’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the Applicant to come before the Planning
Commission to speak about the project.
  7
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes

Mr. Chima Chibueze, addressed the Planning Commission.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any

Commissioner Fowler asked the Applicant –

 Have you had an occasion where you have had to work on your

  - Mr. Chibueze responded to Commissioner Rice’s questions.

Commissioner Trejo commented that the design of the mural is very
nice. She stated she was getting background in order to see how
we can enhance the design of the mural itself.
Commissioner Trejo asked the Applicant –
 Did you say the Mural has a screen on it?
  - Mr. Chibueze responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams commented that it is a very beautiful
mural.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant –
 Tell me what this art is saying?
 Is this West Africa?
 Does the green color represent war?
